changelog: First recommendations logged (the `bets` table). Stakes are fractional-Kelly shares of a notional bankroll.
Analyst review: a bet needs at least +2c EV per $1 and no favourite shorter than -300; repeated sightings of one price count once; NHL totals include the overtime goal.
Daily SHA-256 manifests of every report begin in the public mirror (reports released after 7 days).
Soccer handicaps and totals Paused after losing to the close; Dixon-Coles replacement pending.
An exchange side with an empty ask book gets no assumed price (two phantom Kalshi dry orders were found and voided). This record page built; the mirror's manifests become append-only.

Closing benchmark for spreads and totals changed, and every past bet restated. Until now the "close" for a spread or total was our own model's distribution applied to the consensus closing line; a study found it leaned toward our side by about half a point, so spread and total CLV read positive when it was not: on the 80 bets whose line two other books had posted, +0.44 reported became -1.10 (24% beat the close); over every bet with a close, golf included, the headline went from +0.47 to +0.06. The close is now the other books' de-vigged prices at the bet's own line in the last pre-kickoff snapshot (our book excluded, Pinnacle weighted 4x). Where fewer than two other books posted that line the old method remains and the row is marked †. Moneyline CLV was never affected. The haircut that shrinks our edges is now fitted against the close only (never on 0/1 outcomes) and moves faster (prior weight 300 -> 100 games).

Pricing and grading changed after a study of 99,000 soft-book prices against the close, and every past bet restated. (1) Exchange prices (Kalshi, Polymarket) leave the consensus a book is judged against: they were inside it, contrary to the published method. (2) A spread or total is now priced against the other books' prices at the same line when at least three post it, instead of our own distribution's translation of the consensus line; the study found this benchmark's EV predicts closing-line value (55-76% of its 2c+ prices beat the close) where the translated one did not. (3) The moneyline close is the other sportsbooks' de-vigged closing prices, our own book and the exchanges excluded, Pinnacle 4x (the stored consensus had included both). (4) Soccer's three-way consensus is weighted like every other market (Pinnacle 4x; it was an unweighted mean). (5) Feed hygiene: totals outside a sport's range, spread prices without a line and two-way prices summing past 112% are discarded before pricing. The headline also states the record without golf outrights, whose tiny long-shot stakes make flat ROI misleading; golf itself is on hold until four tournaments are graded.

DraftKings and BetMGM join FanDuel, BetRivers and Kalshi as the books bets are recommended at (accounts opened today). Prices at the two were already collected and graded, so their haircuts start from learned values, not the default. Earlier bets are not restated: a price there was never recommended. Housekeeping: for one day (Oct 16) ESPN spelt DraftKings "Draft Kings" and the feed stored it as a second book; those rows are merged.

Display only, nothing restated: bets whose fair chance moved six or more points of win probability between the price we took (vig removed) and the close are marked ⁿ as news moves (an injury or lineup change, not drift), and every CLV figure is also shown without them. Only a market close can earn the mark: against the model-translated close (†) a gap is our own model's disagreement. They stay in every total, the headline and the market status: the money was real either way. The split tells a sound method with bad news luck from one that is wrong.

Straight spreads and totals need at least +4c EV per $1 (moneylines stay at +2c). Flagged spread and total prices at the owner's books had lost about 1.3 points of win chance to the market close (about 70 graded), moneylines were +0.56 (65); an Oct 29 study found 2-3c prices at the rung ran +0.10 CLV and 3-5c +0.91. Earlier recommendations are not restated; the learning loop keeps recording from +2c.

Two recommendations removed as data errors: BetMGM's AR-Pine Bluff @ Arkansas moneyline arrived with home and away swapped, which made AR-Pine Bluff +8000 (FanDuel) and Arkansas +3300 (BetMGM) read as +5,267c and +2,169c per $1 in the 6:26 AM college basketball report. Edges over 20 points of win chance are now treated as bad data and never recommended.
